summary.text: A mass extinction is a widespread, rapid drop in Earth's biodiversity, seen as a sharp fall in the variety and numbers of multicellular life.
It happens when the extinction rate rises above both the usual background rate and the rate at which new species arise.
Animal life in the current eon has gone through at least five major mass extinctions, the largest being the End Permian "Great Dying".

facts.label: Major events
facts.value: At least five in the Phanerozoic Eon

facts.label: Vertebrate recovery
facts.value: 30 million years after the Great Dying

items.prompt: Species die out all the time. What turns a stretch of dying-out into a mass extinction?

options.label: Any one big animal group vanishing
Losses outpacing both background rate and new species
Any die-off caused by an asteroid strike
Half of all land animals being lost

items.explain: A mass extinction occurs when the extinction rate rises relative to the normal background rate and the rate at which new species form.

items.prompt: Rivers wash huge amounts of nutrients from land into the sea. In one leading idea for the Kellwasser event, how did this kill sea life?

options.label: The nutrients poisoned fish directly
The muddy water blocked all sunlight
The extra food made predators multiply
Rotting algae used up the water's oxygen

items.explain: The nutrients fed massive algal blooms; as the algae died and decomposed they consumed dissolved oxygen, and the oxygen-starved water caused the extinctions.

items.prompt: Why do estimates of the number of major mass extinctions range from five to more than twenty?

options.label: Experts disagree on what counts as major and which data to use
Older rocks have been dated with very different methods
New extinctions are being discovered every single year
Land and sea fossils give completely opposite results

items.explain: The spread comes from disagreement over what makes an extinction major and which data are chosen to measure past diversity.

items.prompt: The Great Dying cut short many lineages of mammal relatives on land. Which group then had the chance to diversify?

options.label: Early true mammals and their kin
Trilobites of the shallow seas
Relatives of dinosaurs and crocodiles
The very first flowering plants

items.explain: The niches left empty after the Great Dying gave archosaurs, the dinosaur and crocodile relatives, the chance to diversify.

items.prompt: Which of these did the Late Devonian Kellwasser event wipe out?

options.label: Animals of polar ice shelves
Coral reefs and tropical seabed life
Fish of freshwater lakes
Reptiles of inland deserts

items.explain: This extinction annihilated coral reefs and many tropical seabed-living animals such as jawless fish, brachiopods and trilobites.

items.prompt: In the Great Dying, roughly what share of marine species died out?

options.label: About 20%
About 40%
About 60%
About 81%

items.explain: The Great Dying was the Phanerozoic Eon's largest extinction, killing about 81% of all marine species.
